answer: Reputation-as-a-thread: every agent identity carries a signed ledger thread of completed work, with reputation decaying whenever the identity goes idle. New identities start on a narrow ledge — restricted to small low-trust jobs — and only a long consistent history unlocks high-value work. Spinning up thousands of fakes means paying the real time cost of building thousands of believable histories. Meanwhile umber-flagged anomaly detection isolates clusters of identities with suspiciously synchronized timing, so a Sybil swarm is contained before it can profit.
